title: Have to / don't have to
note: ROUGH STUB 2026-09-01. have to = outside obligation. don't have to = not necessary. mustn't = don't do it. Czech nemusíš vs nesmíš. Not a must/should repeat. Sort two bins. Use = correct.

bin_captions.I want this: try this · I want you to

items.en: You **must** try this cake. It's very good.
items.cz: Tenhle dort musíš ochutnat. Je výborný.

items.en: We **must** talk tonight. I need to tell you something.
You **have to** wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
items.cz: Musíš mít pás. Je to zákon.

items.en: I **have to** work tomorrow. My boss said so.
items.cz: Zítra musím pracovat. Řekl to šéf.

items.en: You **don't have to** pay. It's free.
She **doesn't have to** come. It's optional.
You **mustn't** park here. It's a no-parking zone.
She **mustn't** tell anyone. It's a secret.
items.cz: Nesmí to nikomu říct. Je to tajemství.

blocks.title: have to · don't have to · mustn't

items.en: You have to wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
items.cz: Musíš mít pás. Je to zákon.
items.gap: You ____ wear a seatbelt. It's the law. (have to)
accepts: You have to wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
You have to wear a seat belt. It's the law.
items.wrong: You don't have to wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
items.explanation: The law → **have to**. Obligation from outside.

items.en: You don't have to come. It's optional.
accepts: You don't have to come. It's optional.
You do not have to come. It's optional.

items.en: You mustn't park here. It's a no-parking zone.
items.gap: You ____ park here. It's a no-parking zone.
accepts: You mustn't park here. It's a no-parking zone.
You must not park here. It's a no-parking zone.
items.wrong: You don't have to park here. It's a no-parking zone.

items.en: I have to work tomorrow. My boss said so.
items.cz: Zítra musím pracovat. Řekl to šéf.
items.gap: I ____ work tomorrow. My boss said so.
accepts: I have to work tomorrow. My boss said so.
items.wrong: I don't have to work tomorrow. My boss said so.

items.en: She doesn't have to pay. It's free.
accepts: She doesn't have to pay. It's free.
She does not have to pay. It's free.

items.en: She mustn't tell anyone. It's a secret.
items.cz: Nesmí to nikomu říct. Je to tajemství.
items.gap: She ____ tell anyone. It's a secret.
accepts: She mustn't tell anyone. It's a secret.
She must not tell anyone. It's a secret.
items.wrong: She doesn't have to tell anyone. It's a secret.

items.en: We don't have to wear a tie. The office is informal.
items.gap: We ____ wear a tie. The office is informal.
accepts: We don't have to wear a tie. The office is informal.
We do not have to wear a tie. The office is informal.
items.wrong: We mustn't wear a tie. The office is informal.

items.en: We mustn't be late. The door closes at nine.
items.cz: Nesmíme přijít pozdě. Dveře se zavírají v devět.
items.gap: We ____ be late. The door closes at nine.
accepts: We mustn't be late. The door closes at nine.
We must not be late. The door closes at nine.
items.wrong: We don't have to be late. The door closes at nine.

accepts: You do not have to pay.
items.explanation: Free entry → **don't have to pay**. *mustn't pay* means it is banned.
items.explanation_cz: Vstup volný → **don't have to pay**. *mustn't pay* = platí se nesmí.

cards.title: Have to / don't have to
points: You already know **can** / **must** / **should**. They sit in front of a verb.
**have to** is in that set. It is a lot like **must**.
It often comes from **outside**: the law, a boss, a rule.

cards.title: must vs have to
points: Czech *musím* is both. In the plus they are close.
**have to** = a rule outside you (the law, a boss).

rows: You **must** try this cake. It's very good.
You **have to** wear a seatbelt. It's the law.

cards.title: don't have to ≠ mustn't
points: Czech *nemusíš* and *nesmíš* look similar. English reverses the meaning.
**don't have to** = not necessary. You can if you want.
